The labeling workflow is structured as a sequence of deterministic steps: manifest generation, local review, policy-compliant storage, and cost tracking. The Zod-backed schema ensures type safety and consistency across manifests. The absence of AWS integration implies a closed-loop system where all operations occur within local compute. The cost simulator operates under explicit flags that distinguish local from vendor-based workflows. Policy gates enforce temporal and legal constraints on label persistence. These primitives form a compositional logic where each step is conditionally dependent on prior outcomes. Failure modes include schema validation errors, policy violations, or incorrect flag usage. Dualities emerge in the distinction between simulated and actual costs, and between local and external workflows. The system exhibits robustness through layered checks but lacks scalability without vendor integration.
